title: China loan for the Lagos–Ibadan railway
summary: A $1.27 billion loan from China's Export-Import Bank, plus Nigerian government counterpart funds, paid for a 156 km double-track standard gauge railway between Lagos and Ibadan. The line was commissioned in June 2021 and is in use.
simple: Nigeria borrowed from a Chinese state bank to build a modern railway from Lagos to Ibadan. The train is running. Nigeria still has to pay the loan back.

verdict.text: Nigeria is still repaying the loan

gaps: We could not find a final audited project cost. Published figures range from $1.5 billion to $1.6 billion, while the financing we can identify comes to about $1.45 billion.
We could not find public figures for how much of the loan has been repaid so far.
Ridership and revenue figures are not published regularly.

timeline.text: China Eximbank and Nigeria sign a $1,267,317,586 loan.
A limited paid passenger service starts (one return trip a day).
The President formally opens the line.

nodes.label: China's Export-Import Bank (loan)
nodes.simple: A Chinese state bank lent Nigeria $1.27 billion. Nigeria must repay it with interest.
nodes.description: A preferential buyer's credit signed on 18 August 2017. Nigeria must repay it with interest.

nodes.label: Nigeria's own contribution
nodes.simple: Nigeria added about $182 million of its own money.
nodes.description: Nigeria's own contribution, reported at about $182 million. Other reports round it to $200 million.

nodes.label: Lagos–Ibadan railway (156 km)
nodes.simple: The Lagos–Ibadan train has been running since 2021 (a limited service started in December 2020).
nodes.description: A double-track standard gauge railway. A limited paid service started on 7 December 2020, and the line was formally opened on 10 June 2021. It is part of a planned Lagos–Kano railway.
